Practised factorising x² + px + q by finding two numbers with the required sum and product.
Arjun solved 5 of 7 attempts unaided.
They expanded brackets to verify the middle and constant terms.
They correctly identified that x² + x + 1 cannot be factorised using integer pairs.
The coefficient-copying mix-up was corrected later by checking sum and product.
end.parentNote: Arjun practised finding a pair of numbers whose sum matches the middle coefficient and whose product matches the constant term. They used expansion to verify answers, including negative pairs, and later corrected the mix-up of writing the coefficients directly in the brackets. At home, practise a few examples by writing “sum check” and “product check” before finalising each factorisation.
